properties.name: A revising write keeps the value it would otherwise make unrecoverable — and only then
properties.rationale:
Anthony's word, 2026-09-01, accepting the recommendation AND its stated counter-argument: snapshot only when it would actually lose something, rather than on every write.

FROM musicjug (`fact:the-revision-warning-holds-the-only-copy-of-what-it-warns-was-lost`): the warning is emitted by the one caller that could still save the value, and offers an undo recipe instead. The order it prescribed — record_change BEFORE the edit — is not reliably achievable from a harness that emits parallel tool batches, so resting the guarantee on call ORDER rests it on something an agent host can break without either party choosing to. This moves the guarantee inside the write.

⭐ AND IT HAPPENED TWICE TO THE SESSIONS RECORDING IT — on 2026-08-31, and again on 2026-09-01 when sharpening a decision genuinely dropped two paragraphs, recoverable only because the prior value was echoed in the tool reply and the session was still reading it. That second one is the argument in one line.

🛑 BEST-EFFORT BY DESIGN, AND THAT IS NOT LAZINESS. Every error is swallowed into `Preserved::Failed` rather than returned: the write is what the caller asked for, and an improvement that can refuse the original request is a worse trade than the loss it prevents. When the preserve fails the note reports the loss exactly as before — strictly no worse than the old behaviour, so this can only add safety. It also disarms the one landmine in the standing-epoch choice: `MAX_SNAPSHOT_REVISIONS` caps snapshots per node per epoch, and a hot node would otherwise start refusing ordinary writes years from now.

Pinned by three tests written first and OBSERVED FAILING IN THE RIGHT SPLIT: the one that had to change failed, and BOTH counterweights passed against the unfixed code. The counterweights are what make "scoped" mean something — a write replacing nothing preserves nothing, and a field already preserved is not preserved twice. Without them this change would be indistinguishable from snapshotting everything, which is the cost the scope exists to avoid.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
`DesignGraph::preserve_prior_state` in temporal.rs, called from `preserve_prior` in capture.rs at all six revising constructors, BEFORE `revision_of` computes its note.

THE TRIGGER IS NOT A NEW JUDGEMENT. `prior_state_coverage` already computed exactly this condition and the write was already REPORTING it afterwards — "no snapshot holds the prior value, checked, not assumed". All that changed is that the call holding the only copy now keeps it instead of describing its loss. Nothing at risk means nothing taken: a write that replaces nothing, or replaces something already preserved, snapshots nothing.

⭐ IT RUNS BEFORE THE NOTE IS COMPUTED, deliberately. Preserving afterwards would leave the caller reading "no snapshot holds this" about a value that had just been saved — true when computed, misleading when read. Run first and the same note becomes the receipt musicjug asked for, computed rather than claimed.

SUPPORTING CHANGES: `snapshot_node` now delegates to a new `snapshot_state`, which preserves a state the caller supplies rather than one read from the graph — the automatic preserve only learns a field was at risk by comparing incoming values against stored ones, and by then the store holds the new state. Edges are still read live, which is correct because a property-only revision does not move them, and the doc says so rather than pretending to be a general time machine.

A standing epoch `epoch:preserved-on-write` holds these, created lazily. An epoch bounds a round of WORK, and a preserve taken because a write would have lost something is not part of anybody's round; attaching it to whichever epoch was newest would misattribute it, and minting one per preserve would bury a timeline that already has 193.
